findings.text: New beer-and-wine licenses (Type 41 or 42) are non-quota and issued directly by ABC, typically taking 60–120 days if unprotested, but undue-concentration census tracts require a PCN letter from the city and can add 1–3 months.

Full-liquor licenses (Type 47 restaurant or Type 48 bar) are quota licenses in San Francisco and must be purchased on the open market at prices ranging from $100,000 to $450,000, then transferred through ABC in a process that takes 90–240 days including escrow and local zoning sign-off.

conditions: Additional Project Authorization: The Project Sponsor must obtain a Certificate of Appropriateness under Article 10 of the Planning Code for physical alterations to historically significant interior and exterior spaces and features. Additionally, the Project requires adoption of Planning Code Text Amendments to conditionally allow nighttime entertainment on second stories of buildings in the Castro Street NCD Zoning District and to exempt Article 10 Landmark properties from the non-residential use size limits in the Castro Street NCD Zoning District.

Noise, Ambient: Interior occupiable spaces shall be insulated from ambient noise levels. Specifically, in areas identified by the Environmental Protection Element, Map 1, “Background Noise Levels,” of the General Plan that exceed the thresholds of Article 29 in the Police Code, new developments shall install and maintain glazing rated to a level that insulates interior occupiable areas from Background Noise and compl iesy with California Title 24 energy standards.

Use (A): No fewer than 75 days of each calendar year must include the presentation of either a feature-length film or a series of short films with total combined length that is comparable to a feature-length film.

Use (B): In order to ensure that the facility continues to contribute to the cultural richness of the neighborhood and the viability of surrounding small businesses, no fewer than 180 days of each calendar year must include events that are open to the general public or to private parties. No fewer than 90 of those days must include events that are open to the general public, including events for which tickets are available for purchase by the public. The required number of days in this Condition Number 16(B) includes the number of days listed in Condition Number 16(A) above.

Use (C): On an ongoing basis, the operator of the facility shall seek guidance on the overall programming of the facility from one or more San Francisco-based LGBTQIA+ nonprofit organizations or nonprofit film exhibition organizations in order to meet its commitment as stated in the online community benefits package as of June 15, 2023 to have 25% of the programming be related to LGBTQIA art, artists, culture, and activities.

Use (D): In order to meet its commitment as stated in the online community benefits package as of June 15, 2023, to have 25% of the programming be related to LGBTQIA art, artists, culture, and activities, each calendar year following the certificate of occupancy, the operator of the facility shall host one meeting and invited representatives of interested organizations, such as the Castrol LGBTQ Cultural District, the Castro Merchants Association, and others.

Use (E): The operator of the facility shall make ongoing good faith efforts to source a portion of its food or beverage concessions from local businesses located within the Castro LGBTQ Cultural District or up to a quarter mile outside the district’s boundaries, on a rotating basis and in collaboration with the Castro Merchants Association.

Use (F): No later than March 31 of each calendar year, the operator of the facility shall provide to the Director of Planning a written report that (1) lists each event at the facility during the previous calendar year, and (2) describes compliance with all provisi ons of this Condition Number 16 during the previous calendar year. The director shall forward this report to the Historic Preservation Commission.

Nighttime Entertainment: The Nighttime Entertainment shall be performed within the enclosed building only. The building shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building and fixed -source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels specified in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance. Bass and vibrations shall also be contained within the enclosed structure.

Validity: The authorization and right vested by virtue of this action is valid for three (3) years from the effective date that of the Planning Code text amendment become effective. The Department of Building Inspection shall have issued a Building Permit or Site Permit to construct the project and/or commence the approved use within this three-year period. (standard)

Expiration and Renewal: Should a Building or Site Permit be sought after the three (3) year period has lapsed, the project sponsor must seek a renewal of this Authorization by filing an application for an amendment to the original Authorization or a new application for Authorization. Should the project sponsor decline to so file, and decline to withdraw the permit application, the Commission shall conduct a public hearing in order to consider the revocation of the Authorization. (standard)

Diligent Pursuit: Once a site or Building Permit has been issued, construction must commence within the timeframe required by the Department of Building Inspection and be continued diligently to completion. Failure to do so shall be grounds for the Commission to consider revoking the approval if more than three (3) years have passed since the date that the Planning Code text amendment(s) and/or Zoning Map amendment(s) became effective. (standard)

Extension: All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay. (standard)

Conformity with Current Law: No application for Building Permit, Site Permit, or other entitlement shall be approved unless it complies with all applicable provisions of City Codes in effect at the time of such approval. (standard)

Final Materials: The Project Sponsor shall continue to work with the Planning Department on the building design. Final materials, glazing, color, texture, landscaping, and detailing shall be subject to Department staff review and approval. The architectural addenda shall be reviewed and approved by the Planning Department prior to issuance. (standard)

Garbage, Composting and Recycling Storage: Space for the collection and storage of garbage, composting, and recycling shall be provided within enclosed areas on the property and clearly labeled and illustrated on the building permit plans. Space for the collection and storage of recyclable and compostable materials that meets the size, location, accessibility and other standards specified by the San Francisco Recycling Program shall be provided at the ground level of the buildings. (standard)

Rooftop Mechanical Equipment: Pursuant to Planning Code 141, t he Project Sponsor shall submit a roof plan to the Planning Department prio r to Planning approval of the building permit application . Rooftop mechanical equipment, if any is proposed as part of the Project, is required to be screened so as not to be visible from any point at or below the roof level of the subject building. (standard)

Noise: Plans submitted with the building permit application for the approved project shall incorporate acoustical insulation and other sound proofing measures to control noise. Parking and Traffic (standard)

Managing Traffic During Construction: The Project Sponsor and construction contractor(s) shall coordinate with the Traffic Engineering and Transit Divisions of the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA), the Police Department, the Fire Department, the Planning Department, and other construction contractor(s) for any concurrent nearby Projects to manage traffic congestion and pedestrian circulation effects during construction of the Project. Monitoring - After Entitlement (standard)

Enforcement: Violation of any of the Planning Department conditions of approval contained in this Motion or of any other provisions of Planning Code applicable to this Project shall be subject to the enforcement procedures and administrative penalties set forth under Planning C ode Section 176 or Section 176.1 . The Planning Department may also refer the violation complaints to other city departments and agencies for appropriate enforcement action under their jurisdiction. (standard)

Monitoring: The Project requires monitoring of the conditions of approval in this Motion. The Project Sponsor or the subsequent responsible parties for the Project shall pay fees as established under Planning Code Section 3501(e) (1) and work with the Planning Department (standard)

Revocation due to Violation of Conditions: Should implementation of this Project result in complaints from interested property owners, residents, or commercial lessees which are not resolved by the Project Sponsor and found to be in violation of the Planning Code and/or the specific conditions of approval for the Project as set forth in Exhibit A of this Motion, the Zoning Administrator shall refer such complaints to the Commission, after which it may hold a public hearing on the matter to consider revocation of this authorization. Operation (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (A): The business operator shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Street and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. In additio n, the operator shall be responsible for daily monitoring of the sidewalk within a one-block radius of the subject business to maintain the sidewalk free of paper or other litter associated with the business during business hours, in accordance with Article 1, Section 34 of the San Francisco Police Code. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (B): When located within an enclosed space, the premises shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed -source equipment nois e shall not exceed the decibel levels specified in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (C): While it is inevitable that some low level of odor may be detectable to nearby residents and passersby, appropriate odor control equipment shall be installed in conformance with the approved plans and maintained to prevent any significant noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (D): Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company. Trash shall be contained and disposed of pursuant to garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines set forth by the Department of Public Works. (standard)

Sidewalk Maintenance: The Project Sponsor shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. (standard)

Community Liaison: Prior to issuance of a building permit to construct the project and implement the approved use, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties. The Project Sponsor shall provide the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups for the area with written notice of the name, business address, and telephone number of the community liaison. (standard)

Notices Posted at Bars and Entertainment Venues: Notices urging patrons to leave the establishment and neighborhood in a quiet, peaceful, and orderly fashion and to not litter or block driveways in the neighborhood, shall be well-lit and prominently displayed at all entrances to and exits from the establishment. (standard)

Lighting: All Project lighting shall be directed onto the Project site and immediately surrounding sidewalk area only, and designed and managed so as not to be a nuisance to adjacent residents. Nighttime lighting shall be the minimum necessary to ensure safety, but shall in no case be directed so as to constitute a nuisance to any surrounding property. (standard)
comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved June 2023 for the Castro Theatre (429 Castro, 152 m away), establishing a new bar use and nighttime entertainment in a landmark building in the Castro NCD. The Commission imposed extensive noise insulation and community-benefit conditions.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved a major new bar use in the heart of the Castro despite its extreme license density, but required soundproofing to contain bass and vibrations, posted patron-conduct notices, community liaison appointment, and annual reporting. A 4-2 vote signals mixed sentiment even for a cultural landmark.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved June 2012 for 4141–4149 18th St (The Edge), 43 m away. Authorized a place of entertainment as an accessory use to an existing bar—live entertainment added to a nonconforming bar on this same block.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved entertainment uses accessory to an existing bar via CUA, showing that the Commission will layer additional uses onto a nonconforming bar in this district when properly conditioned. No extracted conditions available, but the approval itself is the signal.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved Aug 1999 for Badlands (4117–4121 18th St, 55 m away) to permit dancing on the premises of an existing bar in the Castro NCD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A CUA was required to add dancing to an existing bar, reinforcing the pattern that any expansion of bar activities—especially dancing—needs Commission approval in the Castro NCD even when the bar is a legal nonconforming use.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA approved July 1995 at 465–469 Castro (118 m away, also Castro NCD) to expand an existing bar and convert upstairs space to a bed-and-breakfast use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved a bar expansion in the Castro NCD in 1995, showing that enlargements of nonconforming bar uses can be authorized via CUA. However, two later applications at the same address—extended hours in 1994 (denied) and an outdoor area in 1999 (denied)—show that expansions and intensifications face real scrutiny.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA denied Dec 1994 at 465–469 Castro (118 m away) for extended hours of operation for an existing bar in the Castro NCD. One of only two denials in the candidate set.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission denied a request to extend hours at a Castro bar in 1994. Combined with the 1999 denial of an outdoor area at a nearby address, it shows the Commission will reject intensifications that push beyond the existing nonconforming use envelope, even in this entertainment-heavy corridor.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA denied June 1999 at 454–456 Castro (76 m away) for an outdoor activity area behind an existing full bar in the Castro NCD. The second denial in the candidate set.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Outdoor drinking areas face a high bar in the Castro: this proposal was denied even though the bar itself was legal. The denial signals sensitivity to spillover effects and residential proximity, a concern that will apply to any expansion of the subject bar's footprint or outdoor service.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Continuation of existing bar permitted at the subject site (4146 18th St) in 2004 per Planning Code Section 186, a routine agency referral approving the nonconforming use for ownership change.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: An agency referral showing that ownership changes and continuations of the existing bar at this exact address are routinely approved without a hearing when the use and footprint remain unchanged.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral approved Oct 2011 for an existing nonconforming bar at 4149 18th St (43 m away, same block), change of ownership only, per Planning Code Section 186.1.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Another routine approval of a nonconforming bar on this block for ownership change, reinforcing that maintenance of the status quo is permitted but changes to the use require a CUA.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Use decision approved Feb 2009 at 456 Castro (76 m away) for continuation of an existing bar use as nonconforming, with explicit 'no expansion' notation.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning repeatedly approves nonconforming bars in the Castro NCD but explicitly conditions them with 'no expansion' language, establishing that any increase in bar area or intensity requires a CUA.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a written zoning determination from SF Planning Department before filing any application.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a request to the Zoning Administrator asking: (1) whether merging storefronts 4146 and 4150 18th St and enlarging the existing bar at 4146 into 4150 constitutes an expansion of the existing nonconforming use that requires a CUA under Planning Code Section 178, or a new bar use; (2) whether the occupant count (under or over 50 people), floor area (under or over 2,000 sq ft), and formula-retail status affect the pathway; (3) whether the existing Type 48 license at 4146 can be extended to cover the merged space or a new license is required. Request confirmation in writing before paying any application or permit fees.

filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization (LLC, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (corporation, $100) online. Within 90 days file the Statement of Information ($20 LLC, $25 corporation). Apply for an EIN (free, issued immediately Mon–Fri). The EIN is needed for the bank account and ABC application.

filing_playbook.action: Register for a San Francisco Business Registration Certificate and obtain a California Seller's Permit.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector within 30 days of starting business; the fee is tiered by gross receipts ($55 up to $100k, $95 up to $250k, etc.). The registration year runs April 1 to March 31. Apply for a California Seller's Permit (free) at the CDTFA online portal; it is required before ABC will process a license application. Every other city department asks for your Business Account Number, so complete this step before filing with Planning or DPH.

Banks and ABC require the filed statement. Total cost ~$60–$120.

timeline_cost.notes: The day and cost ranges are for the Conditional Use Authorization and Health permit to operate (the two approvals in the entitlement path) when they are granted. The CUA filing to hearing takes 120–300 days (catalog entry verified; comparables show 8–353 days for seven approved CUA cases, with the Castro Theatre CUA taking 353 days from filing to approval in June 2023). The health permit takes 14–45 days after plan check and final inspection. The CUA fee for a no-construction project is approximately $3,100 (CPI-adjusted from the 2023–24 schedule); larger projects or projects with construction pay higher fees up to $15,000. The health plan check is $828–$2,500 and the permit to operate application is $470 (FY2026–27 verified rates). ABC license costs are not included because the alcohol row status is insufficient information: a new Type 41 or 42 is $1,000–$1,600 and takes 60–150 days; a transferred Type 47 or 48 costs $100,000–$450,000 for the license itself plus $1,000–$1,600 in ABC fees and takes 90–240 days including escrow. Building permit fees ($800–$15,000) and time (14–120 days) are also excluded because that row's status is insufficient information pending occupancy-group confirmation. These figures assume approval; they are not times or costs to a denial or withdrawal.

records_summary: The records show 4144 18th St comprises two storefronts: 4146 18th St has operated as Toad Hall, a full bar with an active Type 48 license since 1981, continuously approved as a nonconforming use; 4150 18th St has operated as Pasta Panino restaurant with a Type 41 license since 2024. In the Castro Street NCD a new bar use is conditional, requiring a Conditional Use Authorization. This block sits in the heart of the Castro's entertainment corridor with extraordinary density: 39 food and drink businesses within 500 ft (13 of them bars), 28 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft (50 within 1,000 ft), and undue-concentration flagged. Only one dated bar-use decision appears in the last 10 years within 1,000 ft—too few for a rate—but the site history and nearby records show the neighborhood has long accommodated bars as legal nonconforming uses, with multiple approvals for ownership changes, entertainment permits, and expansions.
